newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cerj minimum price published.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cerj minimum price published.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state will sell off its 78 percent stake in power firm Cerj for a minimum price of 499 million reais ($499.2 million) at a privatization auction November 20, a state planning official said.
Cerj's total share capital was valued at 640 million reais ($640 million), the official said.
She said up to 10 million reais ($10 million) of the sale price could be paid in privatization bonds, the rest in cash.

Company employees have the right to buy 10 percent of the share capital held by the state, equivalent to 7.8 percent of the total share capital, with a 30 percent discount on the minimum price, the official said.

The remaining 70.2 percent of shares will be sold off in one single block during a closed envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange for a minimum price of 464.7 million reais ($464.7 million), she said.
The buyers of the controlling stake in Cerj will have to make a public offer, giving Cerj's minority shareholders the option to sell their stakes for the auction price, she said.

The rules of the privatization auction were published September 11. Under the terms, any consortium interested in buying Cerj would have to include a power company with at least 1 million customers, sales of at least 5,000 gigawatts and less than 12 percent energy losses.
Consortia interested in participating in Cerj's auction will have to pre-qualify by November 4.

The power firm supplies 25 percent of Rio de Janeiro state's electricity and serves around 1.2 million customers. The company's turnover has been estimated at 600 million reais ($600 million) for this year.
